title: fix(plugin-detail): RelatedList reads its rows once, after the child definition settles (objectui#10690)
body:
Fixes #10690

`RelatedList` now waits for its child object's definition to settle before it fetches rows. So a mount reads once, and on a multi-valued relationship that one read already uses `$contains`. The triage auto-adjudicated this as B (`5837899985`). Its execution note, verbatim: 「gate `RelatedList`'s fetch on `useSettledSchema(api, dataSource)`, as `object-map` and `object-data-table` do in PR objectui#10688. Flip the DECLARED COST pin to a one-read pin with `$contains` on the first read, and keep its `SINGLE_VALUED` control.」

Dispatched by the `domain:ui` seat 5 PM, claim `5837949980`. Session: `session_01KUxVUa7e39aNjhkKi1gsoy`.

## What changed

- **`packages/plugin-detail/src/RelatedList.tsx`**
  - The definition used to live in a local `useState`, fed by its own effect. It now comes from `useSettledSchema(api ?? '', dataSource)` (`@object-ui/react`, already a peer dependency). The destructure keeps the name `objectSchema`, so every reader now reads the hook's `def`.
  - The fetch effect returns early while `objectSchemaReady` is false. The check sits right after `setLoading(true)`, so the placeholder holds while it waits.
  - The dependency list gains `objectSchemaReady`, a boolean. The definition reaches the query only through `expandKey`, `selectKey` and the arity flag, never by object identity (AGENTS.md #10).
  - Unchanged: the `cancelled` guard, the refused-filter return and the unscoped-fetch return.
  - Prose this change made false is corrected: the arity-flag comment, the `expandKey`, `selectFields` and `selectKey` docs, and the dependency-list comment.
- **`RelatedList.multiValueParentScope-7299.test.tsx`**
  - `DECLARED COST` is flipped to `ONE READ`: one query, carrying `$contains`.
  - The `SINGLE_VALUED` control (`CONTROL — a single-valued relationship keeps bare equality, byte for byte`) is kept unchanged: one bare-equality read.
  - Added: `SETTLES` (no `getObjectSchema`), `SETTLES` (the definition read throws) and `SWITCH` (a switched `api` uses the new object's definition).
  - The raw-URL refusal case now asserts that no request is sent. Its old assertion was the adapter path's declared cost, carried over.
- **`packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.relatedBadgeArity-8882.test.tsx`** (test only)
  - `MEASURED DIFFERENCE — the badge waits for the arity, the rows attempt first` pinned the same ungated double read from the record page. It is flipped to `ONE READ EACH`: one row query and one badge probe, both membership. The comment in `renderAndCollect` is corrected.
  - This file is outside the claim's file surface. See "Scope" below.
- **`.changeset/10690-related-list-reads-once.md`**: a `patch` for `@object-ui/plugin-detail`.

⛔ Not touched:
- `DetailView.tsx` (open PR objectui#8941);
- the add-picker's own definition read, and the lookup-label hydration read (it now reads the hook's `def`, but its code is unchanged);
- every run guard, and the `error` lifecycle.

No new published prop, and no export change.

## The confidence gap the adjudication named

The question: with an adapter that has no `getObjectSchema`, does the list wait for one more definition read before its first paint?

It does not. It settles **synchronously, inside the hook's first effect run**.
- The no-source exit in `useSettledSchema` (`!dataSource || !settleKey || typeof dataSource.getObjectSchema !== 'function'`) runs in `resolve()` before any `await`, and calls `settle(null)` right there.
- No definition read is issued. The gated query goes out in the re-render that follows, inside the mount's own `act()` flush.
- Pinned by `SETTLES — no getObjectSchema: the gate opens inside the mount itself, one read, rows shown`. It reads `find`'s call count right after `render()` returns, with no `await`, and gets 1.
- First paint is unchanged: `loading` starts `true` on the auto-fetch path, before and after.

The cost that remains: with an adapter that has `getObjectSchema`, the row query now waits for that read, where the two used to run at the same time. Children whose definition moves nothing (single-valued, no expandable column, no predicate operand) get their rows one definition round trip later. Children whose definition moves something needed the second read anyway.

NOT MEASURED: wall-clock latency on a live adapter, reason: no live backend in this run.

## PM hypotheses, as measured

- **H1: confirmed.** On the base, the existing pin file ran green, 16 / 16, and its `DECLARED COST` case asserts two reads with bare equality first. The flipped pins on the unchanged source then fail for exactly that reason: `ONE READ` receives `[equality, $contains]`.
- **H2: confirmed.** Every `objectSchema` reader reads the hook's `def`, and the fetch is gated on `ready`. The stranding the old comment named cannot happen, because the hook settles with `null` when there is no `dataSource`, no `getObjectSchema`, no key, or a read that throws. Ablation A (below) shows the `SETTLES` cases fail on a gate that strands.
- **H3: confirmed.** The dependency list gains `objectSchemaReady`, a boolean, and names no object identity. A switched `api` makes `ready` false in that same render, so the query waits for the new definition. On the base, `SWITCH` receives `[equality, $contains]` for the new object: it queried with the previous object's definition first.

## Evidence

Vitest resolves `@object-ui/*` to package `src` (root `vitest.config.mts` alias), and the pin imports `../RelatedList` relatively. So no leg resolves through `dist`, and no rebuild leg applies.

- **Pins on the base**, source untouched and pins written first: `RelatedList.multiValueParentScope-7299`, exit 1, 3 failed / 16 passed.
  - Red: `ONE READ`, `SWITCH` and the raw-URL refusal.
  - Green by design: the two `SETTLES` cases (the base does not strand either) and every control.
- **Reverse verification**, from committed fix `59f1de2`: `RelatedList.tsx` was set to its base blob. The mutation was proven on disk (blob equals base, not head; `objectSchemaReady` count 0 against 5 at head).
  - 7299 pin: exit 1, 3 failed / 16 passed.
  - 8882 file (from `d0502c9`): exit 1, 1 failed / 4 passed. The failure is the rows' `[equality, $contains]`.
  - Restore was `git checkout HEAD -- PATH` under a `trap … EXIT INT TERM`, proven by blob equals HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.
- **Ablation A** (`ablation-replace.mjs`): the gate reads "a schema loaded" instead of "settled" (`!objectSchemaReady || !objectSchema`). Anchor 1 → 0, blob moved. Exit 1, 3 failed / 16 passed. The 3 red are both `SETTLES` cases and `COUNTER-PROBE — no schema at all …`: the pins catch the stranding.
- **Ablation B**: `objectSchemaReady` removed from the dependency list, gate kept. Exit 1, 10 failed / 9 passed. Every list whose settle moves no content key strands: the controls, the counter-probes, both `SETTLES`, `SWITCH` and the raw-URL control. This is why the flag is in the list.
- Both ablations restored with proof (blob `081db4a` equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty). The restored run: exit 0, 19 / 19.

  - `check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`

## Scope: one file outside the claim's surface

The claim lists `RelatedList.tsx`, the 7299 pin and the changeset. The consumer sample found a second pin of the same recorded decision in app-shell, and it goes red on this change. That sample was the 31 `RecordDetailView*` app-shell tests plus 11 more files that reference the list, 42 in all: exit 1, 1 failed / 304 passed.

It was flipped here under the bounded in-place rule, because all four conditions hold:
- it is the same DECLARED COST decision the adjudication reverses;
- the flip shape is the one the adjudication fixed;
- no open PR and no sibling worktree touches the file (the 13 open PRs and five sibling worktrees were read);
- it adds no new gate: vitest and `type-check` on app-shell, both run above.

The seat should add the file to the claim's declared surface.

## Acceptance notes

- A failed definition read is now logged by `useSettledSchema` (`console.error`), where the list used to log its own `console.warn`. No component `error` state moves.
- `plugin-detail/README.md` was re-read. Its `$select` paragraph ("once the child schema has loaded, the fields the row predicates read") stays true, so there is no doc edit.
- The changeset cites the card and the adjudication. Its prose describes a behaviour change on a published component, so a contract review is owed.
